question: What is the function of Alt + F2 in the Linux GNOME desktop environment?

options.text: Toggles between full-screen and windowed mode
Opens the Run Command dialog box

solution:
The correct answer is __**Opens the Run Command dialog box**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alt + F2** is a keyboard shortcut commonly used in the Linux GNOME desktop environment to **open the "Run Command" dialog box**.
 
• The "Run Command" dialog box allows users to quickly launch applications or execute commands without opening a terminal.
 
• This feature is designed for advanced users who prefer keyboard shortcuts for efficiency and speed.
 
• When the dialog box opens, users can type the name of an application, a command, or a script to execute it directly.
 
• It is a widely supported feature in most Linux desktop environments, including GNOME, KDE, and others, with slight variations in functionality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GNOME Desktop Environment**

 
 
• GNOME is a popular open-source desktop environment used in many Linux distributions.
 
• It provides a graphical user interface (GUI) for managing files, applications, and system settings.
 
• GNOME is known for its simplicity, user-friendliness, and modern design.
 
 
 
• **Keyboard Shortcuts in Linux**
 
 
• Keyboard shortcuts are combinations of keys that perform specific functions, improving productivity and accessibility.
 
• Linux environments often allow customization of shortcuts to suit user preferences.
 
• Examples include Ctrl + Alt + T to open a terminal and Alt + Tab to switch between open windows.
 
 
 
• **Run Command Dialog Box**
 
 
• The "Run Command" dialog box is a lightweight tool for launching applications or commands without navigating through menus.
 
• It is particularly useful for experienced users who are familiar with application names or specific commands.
 
• Commands entered in this dialog box are executed in the background, without requiring a terminal window.
 
 
 
• **Other Common Shortcuts in GNOME**
 
 
• Alt + Tab: Switch between open windows.
 
• Ctrl + Alt + T: Open the terminal.
 
• Super (Windows key): Open the Activities Overview.
 
• Alt + F4: Close the current window.
